title: Exclusive: PJ Washington Is Locked and Loaded for GTA 6, "It's Already Downloaded to My System"
htmlContent:
Some NBA players count down the days to the trade deadline. Dallas Mavericks forward PJ Washington is counting down to something else entirely: the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI.

Speaking exclusively with LandonBuford.com about the most anticipated video game release in years, Washington made it clear he will not be scrambling to find a copy on launch day. He handled that a long time ago.

"I already pre-ordered it, a long time ago. It's already downloaded to my system, just waiting for it to come out."

Considering how long gamers have been waiting, that kind of preparation makes sense. Plenty of athletes are watching the clock, but Washington may be one of the most ready.

A Release Date Years in the Making

Rockstar Games' follow-up to Grand Theft Auto V is set to arrive Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026, on PlayStation 5, including the PS5 Pro, and Xbox Series X|S. There is no PC version at launch.

Getting here took patience. The first trailer, released in December 2023, promised a 2025 release. In May 2025, Rockstar pushed the game to May 26, 2026. Then in November 2025 the studio delayed it again, this time by six months, saying the extra time would let the team finish the game with the level of polish fans expect.

Rockstar's launch trailer on Oct. 15, 2026, confirmed the Nov. 19 date once more. Digital preloads opened Nov. 12, which is exactly why Washington can say the game is already sitting on his console. All he needs now is for the clock to strike release time.

What Washington and Everyone Else Will Be Playing

GTA VI takes players back to Vice City, the series' take on Miami, now part of a larger fictional state called Leonida. For the first time in a mainline Grand Theft Auto game, the story centers on a duo, Jason and Lucia, a criminal pair whose relationship drives the narrative.

The game has been one of the most talked-about entertainment releases in years, inside and outside of sports. NBA players have never been shy about their love of consoles, and road trips, long flights and hotel stays give them plenty of downtime to fill.

Balancing the Controller with the Court

Washington's timing is interesting because his basketball calendar is anything but quiet. The 28-year-old former Kentucky standout, the 12th overall pick in the 2019 draft, has been one of the most important pieces of the Mavericks' rotation under first-year head coach Dusty May.

His perimeter shooting has been a major part of what Dallas wants to do this season. Through the first stretch of the 2026–27 campaign, Washington led the Mavericks in made 3-pointers, and he has been putting up roughly 15.8 points and 7.8 rebounds per game while defending multiple positions.

It has been a strong response to an uncertain summer. Washington spent much of the offseason hearing his name in trade rumors, then agreed to a four-year contract extension in September that tied his future to Dallas. Now he is playing like someone comfortable with where he is.

The release lands in the middle of a busy week. The Mavericks host the Golden State Warriors on Wednesday, Nov. 18, the night before the game drops, then face the Los Angeles Clippers on Saturday. Do not expect Washington to pull an all-nighter on a game day, but the off-hours between those matchups might look a little different this week.

Why Athletes Connect with GTA

Grand Theft Auto has been part of pop culture for more than two decades, and many of today's NBA players grew up with it. Players in their mid-to-late 20s, like Washington, were kids when GTA: San Andreas and GTA IV were everywhere, and teenagers when GTA V arrived in 2013.

That shared history is part of why this launch feels like an event. It is not just a new game. It is the next chapter of a series that has been part of hangouts, dorm rooms and team flights for years. For a lot of players, picking up GTA VI is like reconnecting with an old routine.

Ready When the Clock Hits Zero

Washington's comments capture what millions of fans are feeling heading into Nov. 19. After multiple delays and years of trailers, theories and speculation, the wait is almost over.

For Washington, the hard part is done. The game is paid for, downloaded and ready to go. The only thing left is the countdown, and taking care of business on the court first.

If his shooting stays as hot as it has been for Dallas, Washington will have plenty to feel good about when he finally picks up the controller. And if any of his teammates did not plan ahead, they may be asking to borrow his couch this weekend.
excerpt: Dallas Mavericks forward PJ Washington told LandonBuford.com exclusively that he pre-ordered Grand Theft Auto VI long ago and the game is already downloaded to his console, leaving him with nothing to do but wait for the November 19, 2026 launch.
